test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 12 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Twice the present age of X is 9 years less than thrice the present age of Y. At present, X’s father P is twice as old as X, and Y is 9 years younger than her sister Q. If P is 20 years older than Q, then the present age (in years) of Y is
solution:
**Calculation:**

Let the present age of X be x years.

And the present age of Y be y years.

According to question,

⇒ 2x = 3y - 9 

⇒ 3y - 2x = 9 ……………………………(i)

At present,

X’s father P’s age = 2x years

Y’s sister Q’s age = (y + 9) years

According to given condition,

P is 20 years older than Q

⇒ 2x = y + 9 + 20

⇒ 2x - y = 29 ………………………………(ii)

Adding equation (i) and (ii),

⇒ 2y = 38 years

⇒ y = 38/2 = 19 years

**∴ The present age of Y is 19 years.**
